title: Rural Journalists as Co-Designers: A Case Study of the AI Journalism Fellowship
blurb: A three-month participatory program with ten rural women journalists in India built four Hindi-first, voice-enabled WhatsApp bots, showing how co-design surfaces needs conventional research misses.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Sean Blagsvedt, Dev Aggarwal

title: The Case for Eco-cost Labelling of AI inference
blurb: An open-source repository and API to estimate the environmental costs of AI inference, helping consumers, governments and enterprises make informed choices and reduce emissions that disproportionately affect the Global South.
authors: Sean Blagsvedt, Dev Aggarwal, Archana Prasad, Isha Singh

title: Designing AI with Communities: Lessons from the AI Journalism Fellowship
note: Inaugural MDI Conference: Society-Centered Research and Innovation Through Design
blurb: A presentation on AIJF 2026, showcasing how 10 rural women journalists in India experimented with, and how their feedback shaped improvements to the tools.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Chapter 17.3 in the State of AI Ethics Report, Volume 8
note: Chapter in the State of AI Ethics Report, Volume 8
blurb: The chapter, “Who Gets to Shape AI? Building Coalitions for Underrepresented Communities,” appears as Chapter 17.3 in the section “Civil Society – Austerity, Libraries, Coalitions, & Refusal.” It explores how AI literacy can be reimagined as a participatory practice, examining how communities can move from being passive consumers of AI to actively shaping its datasets and tools.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Shaping AI: Ethics, Power and Responsibility
note: Presented at Art of Research Conference 2026
blurb: This paper examines how AI systems reproduce racial bias and proposed culturally grounded, participatory approaches to developing more inclusive and representative AI systems.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Where textile practice meets machine intelligence
note: Presented at Doctoral Consortium, Textile Intersections 2026
blurb: Through projects including Shaping AI, Andal Meets Ada, and LokaLibraries, Archana's Ph.D research explores how community-led participation, heritage knowledge systems, and cultural memory can shape more inclusive and non-extractive AI infrastructures.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Beyond Bias: Participatory & Reflective Approaches to Cultural AI
note: Presented at RICE Workshop, ACM Creativity and Cognition 2026
blurb: This paper positions creative AI as a tool for ethical reflection, collaborative dataset creation, and culturally grounded approaches to inclusive AI design.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Beyond Bias: Evaluating Cultural AI Through Participation and Interpretation
blurb: This paper argues that cultural AI should be judged by more than harm avoidance. It proposes three evaluation dimensions, cultural integrity, participation and agency, and interpretive capacity, and discusses open questions around ownership and cultural extraction. Accepted to the non-archival Culture × AI Workshop at ICML 2026; not presented at the workshop.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: Beyond Bias: Participatory Design for Inclusive AI
note: Presented at Inclusive AI Lab, Data Care Festival 2026
blurb: This research poster for Inclusive AI Lab covered the Beyond Bias initiative, exploring participatory design approaches for more inclusive and culturally grounded generative AI systems.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons

title: AI Across Cultures: Shaping AI
blurb: The paper explored how social inequalities shape access to AI, and why inclusive, community-led approaches are essential for building culturally grounded AI systems. Accepted to the non-archival AI Across Cultures Workshop at CHI 2026; not presented at the workshop. Was presented at Aalto University in November 2026.
authors: Archana Prasad, Isha Singh, Tom Simmons
